system.summary: 6x6 digit square, each letter a vertical pair of digits 1-6 (top over bottom), with some thirty graphic signs for words or names.
system.notes: Pair 12 = w in Dutch and final z in French; rare pairs 53, 61-64 probably misreadings. Graphic signs act as a small nomenclator.

prior_solution.where: G. Lasry solved it independently in 2021, unpublished (private communication, 25 Sept 2026). DECODE status non-decrypted; no decipherment on the images

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
tools: lang/ fr-1750-nospace and nl-modern sense measure

solution.what: Fetched R1892 images and key records R2240, R2233 with the session cookie.
R2240 (four-digit Orange name key) and R2233: R1892 uses only digits 1-6.
Digits 1-6 written as vertical pairs: a 6x6 Polybius-type square.
Two subagents transcribed page 1 (1039 pairs) and page 2 (790 pairs) as TOP+BOTTOM tokens.
Many-to-one quadgram annealing on the Dutch page: collapsed onto e/n.
One-to-one swap annealing with Dutch quadgrams on page 2: 'het rassemblement te zamen te houden', 'officieren'.
Same square applied to page 1 gives French; 54=q, 14=x, 13=y, 12=z(French) adjusted.
Word signs assigned from decrypted context: circle = de (27, all fit), gamma = zich, c-sign = te, G = ik (probable).
Closing and page 2 line 1 re-read at full resolution: 'à mon frère' (44/54 misreadings of 24/52), 'den generaal Bertincy'; line 24 still unalignable.
Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): Lasry wrote that he had independently solved it in 2021 but never published it; kept in the ciphertext-only list with that note.

R2242's word-sign values (page-1 clear text and context) tried at every occurrence of the matching R1892 sign: bar-H = zoo, > = als (alsdan x2), lambda = dat (x3), parallelogram = brief and p1 box = lettre, 8 = zijn (I) adopted.

R2242 values that do not fit R1892's contexts: phi = Frankrijk, S = moeten, Y-cross = zee, x = weinig, cross = mogelyk, check = zonder; ruled out (different shapes under the same transcriber labels, or other words).
f = aan from aan-geboden, aan-geeven, aan-komst (M).

Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken I-II full text searched (Dundas, Osnabrück, rassemblement, Nienburg, Bentinck, gratification) and GS II pp. 886-894 read: R1892 not printed; no. 724 (Prince Frederick at Nienburg, Oct 1795) and nos. 733-734 identify the writer as Prince Frederick in England and date the letter late Nov - early Dec 1795 (before General Dundas's orders of 8 Dec 1795).
Measured with apply.py --measure and ../r2242/measure_sense.py (fr-1750-nospace p1, nl-modern p2): tokens given a value 95.6% -> 96.5% (1,882/1,951); read as sense 88.5% -> 90.1% (1,757/1,951).

Full-resolution re-reading of every token failing the sense test: p1 L02 (ministres), L04 (touchant la), L13 (donner, top digit unwritten), L18 (question); p2 l15 (voorstellingen die: '61' was 11 65 merged), l22 (de reis derwaards te onderneemen).

Writer's single-digit enciphering slips emended where the word admits no other reading (written>read in the transcription, grade M): 11 pairs (les, déclara, soumettre, leur être, question, circonstances x2, indien, ondernee[men] x2).
P = voor (M): [voor]stellingen, [voor]gesteld.

Read as sense, strict (../r2242/measure_sense.py; fr-1750-nospace p1 with 12 = z, nl-modern p2 with y as ij, French closing scored in French): 1,791/1,951 = 91.8% (HEAD) -> 1,818/1,951 = 93.2% (2 Oct signs) -> 1,860/1,954 = 95.2% (3 Oct). Controls pass 8.7% (p1) and 12.0% (p2).
p2 line 24 re-examined again: only the end ('gesteld is geweest') aligns; the middle stays illegible.

Joint LM scoring of the recurring p2 signs (solve_signs.py: each of ~400 candidate words put into every occurrence at once, nl-modern, 20-letter windows), checked against Gedenkstukken phrasing: H, hook, slash, cf, Y-cross, S, Y, 8, psi, phi, 7, cross. No candidate fits every occurrence (e.g. 'zouden' fits the three H-before-willen places but not the rest, nor the French occurrence on p1); none accepted.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1049 tokens, 26 types, fr-modern order 4: reading -1.951 per letter; random keys -7.687 (z 9.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.603 (mean -4.643, z 92.4); annealer on the real text -1.951. Verdict: pass.

Outside contribution reviewed (PR #31, WAINUT, independent reading 11-12 Oct 2026 with Claude subagents): sign-label splits on p2, 15 proposed sign values, heading 'uit Hampton Court', l13 'myn vader', l24 re-read. Strict p2 coverage 816/900 -> 843/900 -> 859/903 reproduced. Controls (review_control.py): their shuffled-values control scores the same; leave-one-out per added value costs 1-8 tokens; per-occurrence LM ranking against a 62-word pool puts the proposed value first at 5 of 47 places. The measure is coverage, not confirmation; all values kept as proposals, key and outcome unchanged. Heading and l24 digit pairs agree with the full-resolution image; l13 not checked.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcriptions and decrypts of both pages; for p2 also WAINUT's relabelled transcriptions and their decryption (new file wainut/decrypt_p2_wainut.txt, written by running wainut/apply.py); key table copied from NOTES to texts/key.md. Lasry's 2021 solution is private and not in the repository.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): decrypt_p1.txt reads as French sentences (reviewed B); decrypt_p2.txt has an open word sign or conjecture in almost every line, relabelled decoded, not read. Class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.967 (tokens with a value) -> 0.539.
DECODE R1892 and R2242 re-fetched logged in: images only (2 and 4), no document, transcription or key sheet.

WAINUT's 12 Oct shape splits checked on rot_IMG_R1892_I9359_P2.jpg: the H label covers a long-dash H (ll. 4, 5, 7, 8) and the I-beam (ll. 4 hook, 15, 20, 21) = l. 9's bar-H zoo; l. 13 fourth pair is 33 (myn vader). Values adopted where they hold at every occurrence: I-beam = zo, G = UE, flat hook = dat, c-symbol = zal, looped stem = uit (UE, dat, zal sense-only, flagged). Not adopted: crossed Y = ik (fails l. 15), gamma = zulks (fails l. 10), cf = zyn, and one-context values.

Page 2 word-divided and built into sentences (texts/p2_reading.md, English p2_en.md): 0.10 plain, 0.60 explicit holes only; look-alike letters 0. The second half reads; ll. 2-12 do not build (two to five open signs per sentence). Kept decoded, not read.

Verification 4: wrote texts/p1_reading.md and p1_en.md from decrypt_p1.txt, word-divided, slips kept or bracketed, unvalued signs as holes. v2_score 0.70 on explicit holes (plain 0.55), hole rate 0.104.

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): the letter is of 1795; texts/p1_reading.md plain 0.55, explicit 0.70; failures are period spellings, names and supplied word endings. Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

Consistency pass (cl): documents[].read for R1892 p2 read -> read in part, matching its texts state (decoded, not read since the reading audit; b31 re-read did not reach the bar) and fraction_read_source (p1 only, 0.539).
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.951; polyphony 0.0; 5 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.951

outcome.method_basis: The 6x6 vertical-digit-pair square was recovered by one-to-one quadgram annealing on the Dutch page 2 and then read the French page 1 unchanged; the Orange keys R2240 and R2233 did not fit, and there is no decipherment on the images.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: cipher tokens of the page that reads as sentences, p1 = 1,054 of 1,954 (apply.py --measure counts); the Dutch postscript p2 (900) is decoded, not read. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.967 = transcription_p1.txt + transcription_p2.txt with STRICT=1 apply.py --measure (3 Oct 2026): 1,889 of 1,954 cipher tokens given an H or M value; p1 1049/1054, p2 840/900.
outcome.notes: All digit pairs map. Read as sense, strict (I values unread): 1,860/1,954 = 95.2% (p1 99.1%, p2 90.7%); 91.8% for the 21 Sept state under the same measure. 11 writer slips emended (listed in NOTES). Passes 95% as a whole by about 4 tokens (1,860 against 1,856.3), but the Dutch postscript (p2) is 90.7% and its recurring word signs are still workable: kept read in part at the write-up update of 3 Oct 2026; reclassed read on 5 Oct 2026 (5 Oct 2026, project rule: a target measured at 95%+ read as sense counts as read in full, open code signs notwithstanding). Writer Prince Frederick, late Nov - early Dec 1795.

texts.label: R1892 page 1 (French)
texts.summary: Prince Frederick of Orange, in England, c. late November - early December 1795, to an officer of the Dutch émigré troops (the 'rassemblement') in British pay: his father is sending Nagell back to the ministers to press for an answer, and if General Dundas declares that the pay will stop or the troops must embark, the recipient is to accept and only try to obtain a gratification for those who will not submit.

reading_review.note: v4 check 23 Oct 2026: decrypt_p1.txt is the unspaced decode, which the scorer could not score. Written out as texts/p1_reading.md (word-divided from the decode, 3 Oct transcription with the eleven slip emendations; remaining slips kept or marked [?word]; dash, bar and H signs unread). v2_score: plain 0.55 (11/20), explicit holes 0.70 (14/20), hole rate 0.104, 241 words; plain is low on 1795 spellings (pouroit, étoit, voudroient). Every sentence holds (Nagel to the ministers; if Dundas stops the pay or orders embarkation, subscribe and seek a gratification; the paper for the troops; the lodging expense). Keeps read, grade B. v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): the letter is of 1795 (the folder is named for DECODE R1892), French: plain bar. texts/p1_reading.md body: plain 0.55 (11/20), explicit holes 0.70 (14/20), hole rate 0.104. The plain failures: 1795 spellings (pouroit, pourez, cesseroit, dépences), names (Nagel, Vundas = Dundas), letters supplied at word ends ('flatte[r]', 'elle[s]', counted as holes) and four unread signs; each sentence builds. Keeps read.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 89.6% of the words of texts/p1_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R1892 page 2 (Dutch postscript): reading adopted here, and the WAINUT proposals
texts.summary: The Dutch postscript, 'in het hollandsch met cijffer': if the troops stay together the rassemblement is to be kept together, volunteers and officers named and employed, and officers who will not serve given a set number of days to choose; the writer has had no answer for weeks to his first letter. wainut/decrypt_p2_wainut.txt applies WAINUT's proposed sign splits and values (12 Oct 2026, not adopted) for comparison.
texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (batch b31; texts/p2_reading.md, p2_en.md, p2_reread_log.md, p2_corrections.tsv): WAINUT's shape splits checked on the image (the H label is two shapes; the I-beam = l. 9's zoo); values adopted only where they hold at every occurrence: I-beam = zo, G = UE, flat hook = dat, c-symbol = zal, looped stem = uit (UE, dat, zal sense-only, flagged); crossed Y = ik fails at l. 15, gamma = zulks at l. 10, so not adopted; l. 13 'myn vader' read on the image. Word-divided reading scores 0.10 plain, 0.60 explicit holes only; look-alike letters 0. Kept decoded, not read: ll. 2-12 carry two to five open signs per sentence (long-dash H, S, 7, Y, bar, x, delta, circle-cross) and do not build; the second half reads.
